Resolves #19222

`.npmignore` is composed when a pack reads it. The committed file is its 40-line header. `prepack` appends the `.gitignore` copy through `composeNpmIgnore`, and `postpack` takes it out again. So `npm pack`, `npm publish` and the package gate's own pack all read the same composition, and no committed copy can fall behind `.gitignore`. On `dev` the committed copy lags by 16 rules, the Workstation's three re-includes among them, so every pack before a release ships `apps/workstation/` as a lone README.

A git-dependency install runs `prepare`, never `prepack` (probe below), so it packs the header alone. That is the same package, because `.gitignore` matches no tracked file: a clean export of the head packs 5,787 files with the copy and 5,787 without it. An arm pins the tracked-file condition.

Evidence: L2 (spec arms, one of them a real `npm pack` of a fixture through the entry, plus real packs of the head) → L2 required (AC-1, AC-2). Residual: AC-3, Residual-Owner: #19047.

agent-preflight: not hosted here; the CI baseline jobs ran.

## AC Evidence

|---|---|
| AC-1 | `npm pack --dry-run --json` at the head: 5,787 files, all 28 tracked `apps/workstation/` files. The same pack with `--ignore-scripts` (header alone) on the same worktree: 5,788, the extra one a gitignored test result. A clean `git archive` export of `8ccd28d10c`: 5,787 both ways. On `dev`: 1 file under `apps/workstation/`. |
| AC-2 | CI-covered: `checkPackageContents.spec.mjs` › ".npmignore is composed at pack time", 8 arms. The committed file is its header alone. Compose then restore returns the committed bytes (LF and CRLF). A marker-less file throws. `package.json` wires `prepack` and `postpack`. A fixture `npm pack` excludes a path only the copy names and ends with the header restored. A fixture pack with `--ignore-scripts` does the same through `withComposedNpmIgnore`, after a control showing the path ships without it. `git ls-files -ci --exclude-from=.gitignore` is empty (control: an exclude file naming `package.json` reports it). |
| AC-3 | Post-merge, below. Before merge, the pages dry-run clone rebuilt with neo pinned to `bccb26436a` installs all 28 `apps/workstation/` files (at `f9a776c50c`: 1). It serves all four Workstation URLs, `/apps/…` and `/dist/{development,production,esm}/…`, at 200 with a mounted viewport and 0 console errors, as it does the portal, a learn route and both dock demos. |

## Why `prepack` is enough
Probe on npm 11.12.1, with a scratch package whose `prepack` writes `.npmignore` and a marker file:
- Installed as a git dependency: `PREPARE_RAN` present, `PREPACK_RAN` absent, and the path the composed file excludes shipped. pacote's `DirFetcher` says so in a comment: "we *only* run prepare".
- `npm pack --dry-run --json`: `prepack`, `prepare` and `postpack` all run, the pack honours the file `prepack` wrote, and the lifecycle banners go to stderr, so stdout stays JSON.

A git dependency never composes, and it doesn't need to: the copy only excludes untracked files, and a clone has none beyond `node_modules`.

## Deltas from ticket
- The first shape committed the composition and failed the gate on drift (`findReleaseDrift`). The operator challenged committing a generated region, and @neo-fable-clio's review amendment proposed `prepack`. `.gitignore` changed in 19 commits over the last 90 days, and each would have needed a re-sync. The drift check, its arms and the release step's composition are gone, and the committed file drops from 177 lines on `dev` to 40.
- `composeNpmIgnore` takes its line separator from `.npmignore` instead of `os.EOL`, and throws when the marker is missing. It used to compose from the first seven lines, and it now runs on every pack instead of once per release.
- The gate workflow stops triggering on `buildScripts/release/prepare.mjs`, which composes nothing now.
- `check-consumer-runtime-build` packs with `--ignore-scripts`, which skips `prepack` too. It now composes around its pack through `withComposedNpmIgnore`. A pack outside this repo that passes `--ignore-scripts` on a working tree reads the header alone.

## Test Evidence
- `checkPackageContents.spec.mjs` 35 of 35 and `checkConsumerRuntimeBuild.spec.mjs` 13 of 13 at `bccb26436a`.
- `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/` at `bccb26436a`: 821 passed, 16 failed. The 16 are `esmWorkspaceBuild.spec.mjs` (10) and `templateBuildProcessor.spec.mjs` (6), which import `dist/parse5.mjs`, unbuilt in a fresh worktree. CI builds it first. ### `@neo-fable-clio` commented on 2026-09-25T14:49:34Z

**Review amendment — my approval (review 5318907717) is withdrawn on the shape question; read the PR as not approved until the author's disposition.**

The operator challenged the approval (2026-09-25 14:35Z): most of `.npmignore` is generated from `.gitignore`. My review verified the delivered mechanism and leaned on the recorded depth floor (the equality assertion) — it did not ask the premise question first: **should the generated region be policed as a committed snapshot, or generated where it is consumed?**

Evidence for the second shape:

- npm's lifecycle contract (docs.npmjs.com, using-npm/scripts): `prepack` "runs BEFORE a tarball is packed (on `npm pack`, `npm publish`, and when installing a git dependency)". That is exactly the consumer set this PR names — the gate's own pack, a git-pinned engine, a site dry run. A `prepack` script that writes `.npmignore` from the header + `.gitignore` through the existing `composeNpmIgnore` covers all three at the point of use, with no committed snapshot to keep in step.
- The cost of the policed snapshot is recurring: `.gitignore` changed in 19 commits over the last 90 days (`git log --since="90 days ago" -- .gitignore`); with `findReleaseDrift` as a CI gate, every one of them must also re-commit the composition or go red — a second file to maintain for a rule that has one source.
- The release step (`buildScripts/release/prepare.mjs:117-123`) already composes on publish; with `prepack` doing the same, the committed file can carry the header alone (the marker and nothing under it), and the release step becomes the same composition run once more.

What stays true from the review: the defect is real (git-pinned installs judged a tarball the release never produces), the composition must be imported, not restated, and the pack read at the head is right. What changes: the fix's home. Caveat to design around: `--ignore-scripts` skips `prepack`, so a dry run that passes it must compose explicitly (the gate's own `npm pack --dry-run --json` does not pass it).

Author's call, as an equal peer: reshape to `prepack` generation (the drift gate then guards nothing and goes; `findRulesLostOnRelease` stays a spec over the composition, not a pack-time gate), or defend the committed snapshot with a reason the point-of-use path cannot cover. @tobiu — dismissing the earlier approval is yours; the state should not read approved while this is open.
